title: React Performance Tracks: see React's work on the timeline

slides.say: Record a trace in your browser's Performance panel, and React adds its own tracks next to network and JavaScript work.

slides.text: Scheduler track: Blocking, Transition, Suspense, Idle. Each render shows Update, Render, Commit, Remaining Effects.
slides.say: The Scheduler track splits work by priority: blocking, transition, suspense, and idle. Each render shows its phases: what triggered it, render, commit, and the remaining effects.

slides.text: Components track: a flamegraph of renders and effects, with Mount and Unmount labels. In dev, click to see changed props.
slides.say: The Components track is a flamegraph of which components rendered, and how long they took. In development, click an entry to see which props changed.

slides.text: Watch for “Cascading update”: an update during render made React throw work away and start again.
slides.say: Look out for cascading updates. That's an update scheduled during a render, which makes React drop finished work and start over.
The tracks are on in development, and off in production because they add overhead. For a production-like trace, use the profiling build of react dom.
